scope.question: Do all three preregistered CAMI novelty distinctions remain unsupported by prior work?
scope.evidence_policy: Paper full text, official proceedings, DOI landing page, or author primary preprint; discovery summaries were not used as final evidence.

closest_prior_work.title: Pctx: Tokenizing Personalized Context for Generative Recommendation
closest_prior_work.status: arXiv preprint; submitted as an ICLR 2026 paper
verified_claims: The same item is assigned multiple Semantic IDs conditioned on full user history.
Training augments sequences by replacing an item SID with another valid SID of the same item.
A single autoregressive encoder-decoder generates alternative SID paths.
At inference, probabilities of distinct SIDs mapping to the same item are aggregated into next-item probabilities.
overlap_with_cami: many identifier paths aggregated to one item
closest_prior_work.remaining_difference: Pctx does not allocate aliases using baseline candidate starvation or evaluate fixed-50 tail candidate recovery.

closest_prior_work.title: PIT: A Dynamic Personalized Item Tokenizer for End-to-End Generative Recommendation
closest_prior_work.status: arXiv preprint with placeholder venue metadata
verified_claims: A dynamic beam index maintains multiple valid SIDs per item.
The User-to-Token generator selects a candidate SID using minimum recommendation loss.
The index implements an inverse mapping from multiple SIDs to one item.
closest_prior_work.remaining_difference: PIT uses minimum-loss selection and targets streaming index stability; it does not use log-sum path marginalization or a fixed-budget tail-recovery claim.

closest_prior_work.title: Pre-training Generative Recommender with Multi-Identifier Item Tokenization
verified_claims: Each item receives multiple identifiers from adjacent RQ-VAE checkpoints.
The identifiers augment pre-training sequences under a curriculum.
Fine-tuning and deployment return to a single tokenizer.
closest_prior_work.remaining_difference: Multiple identifiers are a pre-training augmentation and are not retained or aggregated at inference.

closest_prior_work.title: Multiview Identifiers Enhanced Generative Retrieval
verified_claims: Passages use synthetic identifiers, titles, and substrings as complementary views.
The views are combined for holistic passage ranking.
closest_prior_work.remaining_difference: It is document retrieval, not sequential recommendation, and does not use behavior-conditioned or starvation-adaptive alias allocation.

adaptive_allocation.assessment: No audited work was found that specifically allocates additional valid identifiers only to items selected by candidate-starvation or prefix-congestion evidence.
adaptive_allocation.caveat: Pctx uses a variable number of IDs proportional to context frequency and PIT maintains a dynamic beam index, so this distinction is narrow.

single_decoder_item_marginalization.assessment: Pctx already trains a single autoregressive recommender with multiple valid same-item Semantic IDs and aggregates the probabilities of generated SID paths back to next-item probabilities.

fixed_budget_tail_recovery.assessment: The audited closest works do not frame or gate their contribution as tail candidate recovery under a fixed total decoding budget.

decision.reason: All three gates were necessary. The single-decoder multi-path item aggregation gate is substantively covered by Pctx, and MTGRec/PIT further crowd the multi-identifier design space.
decision.allowed_next_action: Reframe the research question under a new cycle before any data diagnostic or model implementation.
